# 1 Enoch Chapter 65 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** After this, Enoch disappeared. Not one human being knew where he had gone, where he was living, or what had happened to him.

**2** His work had to do with the Watchers, and he spent his time among the holy ones.

**3** I, Enoch, was blessing the Lord of Majesty and the King of all ages when suddenly the Watchers called out to me — Enoch the scribe — and said:

**4** "Enoch, scribe of righteousness! Go and deliver this message to the Watchers of heaven who abandoned the high heaven — the holy and eternal dwelling — defiled themselves with women, did what mortals do, and took human wives: You have brought terrible destruction on the earth.

**5** You will have no peace and no forgiveness of your sin. As for the children you delight in —

**6** you will watch your beloved children be killed, and you will mourn over their destruction, and you will plead and pray forever, but you will never receive mercy or peace."

**7** So Enoch went and delivered the message: "Azazel — you will have no peace. A severe verdict has been issued against you: you will be bound and imprisoned. You will not be tolerated, and no request of yours will be granted, because of the wickedness you taught and all the acts of godlessness, injustice, and sin you demonstrated to humanity."

**8** Then I went and addressed all of them together. They were all terrified; fear and trembling overwhelmed them.

**9** They begged me to compose a petition for them, in hopes of receiving forgiveness, and to read their petition before the Lord of heaven.

**10** Because from that time on they could no longer speak directly to him or even raise their eyes toward heaven — they were too ashamed of the sins for which they had been condemned.

**11** So I wrote out their petition — a prayer about each one's spirit and deeds individually, and their request to receive forgiveness and extended life.

**12** Then I went and settled beside the waters of Dan, in the territory of Dan, to the south and west of Hermon. I read their petition aloud until I fell asleep.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Ch. 65 interrupts the Parables with a scene from the earlier Book of the Watchers — Enoch as the Watchers' petitioner/scribe. This role is developed in ch. 12-16 of the Book of the Watchers. Azazel is named in v. 7 — the only explicit appearance of this name in the Parables. The geography of v. 12 (Dan/Hermon) is the same as ch. 13.*
